overview: This Senate resolution marks the 75th anniversary of the start of the Korean War, which began on June 25, 1950, when North Korea invaded South Korea. It honors the more than 1.7 million Americans who served, including over 36,000 who died, and notes the war's toll on South Korea. It recognizes South Korea as a key U.S. ally and reaffirms the U.S. commitment to a strong, well-prepared military, urging continued investment in training and equipment. It also calls on Americans to remember the conflict not as the "Forgotten War" but as the "Noble War." The Senate agreed to it on June 25, 2025.
for: Supporters say it honors the sacrifice of Korean War veterans, many of whom felt overlooked, and underscores the value of a strong alliance with South Korea.
against: Critics say it is symbolic and does not change any law or provide any funding for the military readiness it calls for.
